The application is built, verified, and ready for your review. Here is the Phase 4 acceptance report.

---

## ✅ Your Link Library is ready to review

**Open it here: http://maker:4000**

It starts as a calm, empty library — paste a link to begin. It's a real working app now (not the exploratory prototype): your links, tags, notes, saved views, and preferences live on the server, so the same library appears on any device you open it from.

### What was built — the 15 behaviours you approved
- **Saving:** paste a link (shorthand like `nytimes.com` works); it fetches the real page's title, description, preview image, icon, and date for you to review and adjust before saving. If a page can't be reached, you fill the details in by hand rather than being blocked. Bad addresses are refused; duplicates take you to the existing entry.
- **Editing:** change title, description, note, tags, reading state, or the address later — an address change re-fetches for review while keeping your own wording.
- **Reading vs. reference**, the temporary "To read" flag, and one unified library.
- **Rediscovery:** tag reuse suggestions, include/exclude tag filters, and the full search language (phrases, `#tag`, case-insensitive `and/or/not`, parentheses), plus a **Markdown note** separate from the page description.
- **Managing at scale:** archive/restore (delete only from the archive, confirmed), sorting, bulk actions with "select all matching," saved views, browser-bookmark import/export (folders → tags), and display preferences (default order, links per page, text size) synced to your library.

### Verification outcome (plain language)
- **Internal quality tests: 19/19 passed** (address rules, search grammar, Markdown safety, bookmark import/export, storage & sync).
- **Behaviour acceptance tests: 23/23 passed**, covering every approved scenario, with **no runtime errors**.
- **Sync confirmed:** the library and preferences persist server-side and are served identically to any device.

### Held to our agreed boundaries
- **Preserved page copies & Internet Archive** are **not** in this build — recorded as a dedicated follow-up cycle (LATER-002). No buttons pretend to preserve.
- Single personal library with cross-device sync; no sharing, multi-user admin, or self-service account management this cycle.

---
